messages:
IncBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: latency SLO breach detected for hosted/generation-streaming (route: /v1/chat/stream). p95 and p99 elevated. Paging ml-oncall.

Maya (ml-oncall): taking, on it. what's the current window?

IncBot: root_ts=3529008765, window=2024-06-12T16:12Z-16:22Z, p95=820ms (SLO=300ms), p99=2.7s (SLO=800ms), streaming stalls reported, error-rate low, but many long-lived responses stall around token 1-4 of continuation.

AJ (infra): seeing CPU pinned on dequant workers on a subset of nodes. mem looks fine. Routing shows traffic skew to quantized-int8-variant-3.

Leo (sre): can we confirm this correlates with yesterday's calibration rollout? I saw a canary promoted at 02:00 UTC.

Sara (runtime): yes, int8-variant-3 was pushed to staged serving pool and then gradually routed. Calibration logs show frequent "dequantize_kv:miss" warnings around the same timeframe.

Tess (support): Customer TODO list: we have two paying Dedicated customers on the route, one reported increased complaints about slow stream starts. I've opened CS ticket #CS-8891 and flagged for SLA.

Maya (ml-oncall): quick triage plan: 1) identify which model variant hosts are seeing highest p99 2) throttle traffic to variant-3 -> route to fallback fp8 or fp32 variant 3) if rollback needed, roll it out and monitor

AJ (infra): running quick query:
```
rk get pods -l variant=int8-variant-3 -o wide
# pod list -> node mapping
```
Nodes n-17 and n-18 show elevated GPU utilization but also long tail of inference loops (runtime stuck in dequant kernel).

Sara (runtime): paste of recent logs (abridged):
```
[2024-06-12T16:15:23Z] dequantize_kv: miss for shard 4
[2024-06-12T16:15:23Z] fallback_queue length 42
[2024-06-12T16:15:24Z] stream: stall at token 3, ctx_len=2048
[2024-06-12T16:15:24Z] kernel_launch: slow 1.2s
```

Leo (sre): streaming stalls at token 1-4 suggests prefix/KV mismatch or calibration causing repeated KV cache evictions. Also seeing increased lock contention in KV cache mutexes.

Maya (ml-oncall): any correlation to request size or long-context sessions? Could be long-context + int8 quantization causing dequant hotspots.

AJ (infra): traffic heatmap: 78% of affected requests have seq_len > 1500 and many are long-lived chat sessions. So yes, long-context correlation is strong.

Tess (support): CS patch: customers on Dedicated saw 40-60% slower median stream start for long prompts. Not yet widespread 5xx, mostly slow responses and user timeouts in client apps.

Maya (ml-oncall): mitigation attempt 1: Do a quick route weight change to reduce traffic to int8-variant-3 by 80%.

AJ (infra): executing routing change now:
```
redwood route update /v1/chat/stream --variant-weight int8-variant-3=20,fp8-variant-1=80
```

IncBot: deploy event recorded by DeployBot at 3529008793. Routing change applied.

Sara (runtime): initial metrics: within 60s, p95 dropped from 820ms -> 410ms, p99 from 2.7s -> 1.1s. Good delta but still above SLO for p99.

Leo (sre): we need to determine if rollback of calibration data on the int8 variant is required or whether we can keep low weight for longer and coordinate a safer re-calibration. Any quick fixes at the model level?

Maya (ml-oncall): quick test: repush calibration with stricter clipping/scale for KV tensors might reduce dequant jitter. But re-calibration is risky mid-prod. I recommend 1) keep low weight, 2) spin up isolated rollback pool for int8-variant-2 (previous calibration) and switch traffic to it if p99 stays high.

AJ (infra): creating a rollback pool with variant-2 now. Pods spawning, will warm caches.

Tess (support): notifying affected customers in CS-8891 that we're mitigating and expect measurable improvement in ~5 minutes. Asking for any session IDs that still fail.

Sara (runtime): confirmation: pod warmup logs show KV caches warming, but we need to ensure cache keyspace alignment; previous variant used a slightly different quantization ordering which could cause cache misses during seamless variant swap. We'll route only new sessions to variant-2 to avoid cross-variant KV mismatch.

Maya (ml-oncall): good call. We'll do 'new-sessions-only' routing to variant-2 for now. Older sessions pinned to existing worker will continue to slowly drain to reduce client disruption.

AJ (infra): applied route rule: new_sessions->fp8-variant-1 (60), int8-variant-2 (40); old sessions sticky -> int8-variant-3 until drain

IncBot: sticky drain count: 1,240 sessions to drain from int8-variant-3. Estimated drain time ~6-9 minutes.

Leo (sre): during drain check for any p99 regressions. If p99 still >1.5s after 10 minutes, escalate to emergency rollback (force all traffic to fp32 fallback).

Sara (runtime): observed behavior as pods switch: lock contention metrics on KV mutexes drop 70%. p95 now 290ms (within SLO), p99 920ms (slightly above target but improving).

Tess (support): customer update sent: "We've routed new sessions to a safer variant and are draining affected workers. You should see much improved stream startup within the next few minutes. We'll follow up once the incident is resolved." :pray:

Maya (ml-oncall): timeline + notes for postmortem: - root cause: calibration change for int8-variant-3 introduced KV quant ordering edge-case causing frequent dequant misses and mutex contention under long-context workloads - detection: routing telemetry alarm p99 spike - mitigation: rapid route-weight change, spawn rollback pool, new-session-only routing, drain - next steps: halt further int8 rolling promotions, run synthetic long-context load against recalibrated variant, improve calibration validation including KV cache-sanity checks and shield long-context heavy routes in future rollouts

Leo (sre): tagging oncall-sre for postmortem. @Maya please open incident ticket with the above and include links to: deploy, routing change, calibration artifact id, CS-8891.

Maya (ml-oncall): will open INC-4522 and assign owners for calibration fixes and improved canary tests. Also scheduling a postmortem meeting at 2024-06-13T15:00Z.

AJ (infra): final check: p95 285ms, p99 700ms. We'll keep monitoring for the next hour. Reverting to normal routing only after 2 hours of steady metrics.

Tess (support): marking customers notified and SLA impact assessed: minor SLA degradation for one hour window, potential credit estimate being prepared.

IncBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, routing adjusted, monitoring watch active. If any team needs escalation, @pagerduty-msk.

Maya (ml-oncall): thanks everyone. I'm leaving the watch with Leo (sre) for next 60m, will be available on DM. If p99 creeps back up, escalate immediately.

Leo (sre): taking watch. continuing metric checks and customer impact thread. :eyes:

-- end of thread --
